title: The Trees and the Axe
summary: Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that giving your enemy the means to hurt your brother leads swiftly to your own destruction.
full_text: Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. A woodman walked into an ancient forest and begged the trees to grant him a single piece of hardwood to fashion a handle for his iron axe head..... The surrounding valley lay quiet in the midday heat, yet within the peaceful scene, natural instincts and rival interests were quietly at work. Before long, the initial quiet gave way to a sharp challenge as unexpected circumstances forced both sides to act. Natural instincts and sharp wits collided, bringing the trial to an immediate, decisive climax. Words of sharp wit and warning were spoken before the final consequence struck. Each party sought to press their advantage, weighing spoken words against unspoken motives. When the decisive moment arrived, neither boastful pretense nor hasty excuses could alter the outcome. The outcome revealed the enduring truth of human character. The experience left behind a timeless truth for all who heard the tale, demonstrating that giving your enemy the means to hurt your brother leads swiftly to your own destruction.
moral: Giving your enemy the means to hurt your brother leads swiftly to your own destruction.
